decision: test target is Chromium driven by Playwright with a phone viewport and 4x CPU throttle, not an Android device
why: no adb, no Android SDK, and Windows reports HypervisorPresent False, so an emulator would need an admin feature install and reboot that should not happen unattended
result: open: native-only numbers (cold start, UI-thread frames) cannot be measured

decision: sent competitor and RSVP research to a subagent limited to primary sources
why: no phones here so no first-hand recordings; the research is independent of the code work
result: open

decision: measured the reader page in throttled Chromium: 5 runs, 3 books, light and dark
why: numbers before any fix, as asked
result: open 484 ms small, 988 ms large; page numbers 50 s on the 10 MB book; 52 of 130 turns drop a frame on it

decision: drove the RSVP engine with a frame clock instead of the real overlay
why: the overlay cannot mount on web until the reader does
result: real speed 265 at a setting of 300; p95 lateness 16.7 ms on a perfect clock

decision: profiled steady page turns on the 10 MB book before changing anything
why: I had guessed the cost was our own page-number lookup; the profile says otherwise
result: getBoundingClientRect 9.9 ms and layout 15 ms per turn inside epub.js position mapping; our lookup under 1 ms; guess dropped

decision: made the reader run on web with an iframe and IndexedDB storage
why: the web build is a declared target, the only one runnable here, and the e2e tests the task asks for need it
result: reader opens on web

decision: fixed a race where the database handle was handed out before its tables existed
why: first import on web failed with no such table: book_files
result: import works

decision: broken EPUB files now report an error
why: a truncated file showed Opening book for ever; epub.js only signals it through an openFailed event
result: error shown with a way back

decision: gave the RSVP engine and overlay changes to a subagent in its own worktree
why: that folder is self-contained and covered by jest, so it could run beside my reader work
result: real speed now equals the setting: 300, 500, 800

decision: replaced the filter themes with painted palettes
why: the filter inverts pictures in dark mode; speed was not the reason, the baseline showed no measurable filter cost
result: e2e checks dark background rgb(28,28,28); not verified on a phone

decision: rewrote ReaderScreen around one chrome state and split out two sheets
why: five booleans, an auto-hide timer, unsaved settings, unreachable bookmarks and three blocking alerts were all in the audit
result: 1889 lines to about 800; 10 of 10 e2e pass

decision: Add opens the picker and then the book; cover tap opens the book
why: import took 6 taps to reach reading
result: 2 taps

evidence: e2e/reader.spec.ts 'speed reading starts on the page being read'
result: passes

decision: tried a slide page turn with CSS smooth scrolling, and did not keep it
why: two quick taps left the page at offset 442 on a 353 px page; epub.js scrolls by a relative amount, so a second turn mid-animation misaligns
result: discarded; a correct version needs a turn queue and a device to judge smoothness

decision: tried loading the next chapter ahead of time, and reverted it
why: chapter-boundary frame gap did not move: p50 66.7 ms and 10 of 10 turns dropping a frame, with and without; I did not confirm epub.js reused the preloaded chapter
result: reverted, no measurable difference

decision: re-ran the reader benchmark on the finished tree: 5 runs, 3 books, light and dark, plus a second open with cached page numbers
why: same harness and books as the baseline
result: page numbers on reopen 0.3/0.7/0.8 s (were 2.4/50.9/8.1 s); open time on the illustrated book up 16%; long-book turns dropping a frame up from about 50 to 73 of 130

decision: started an A/B on hyphenation to explain the two numbers that got worse
why: it is the only change that adds layout work to every page
result: open

decision: re-measured the two numbers that looked worse by alternating the original page and the new page back to back
why: hyphenation A/B showed no difference, so I suspected the measurement before the code
result: no measurable difference: long book 45/78 and 43/78 dropped (old) vs 43/78 and 42/78 (new); the earlier gap was drift between sessions hours apart

decision: measured the real overlay in the web app under 4x throttle
why: the engine harness is not the app
result: frame gap p95 16.7 to 16.8 ms; 2, 1 and 0 frames dropped in 20 s at 300, 500, 800 wpm

decision: measured library scroll at 100, 400 and 1000 books
why: the baseline could not, because the web build could not add books
